newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT-CRICKET-Harris says bowling effort among his best.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-CRICKET-Harris says bowling effort among his best.

text.p: NAPIER, Feb 27 - "Right up there"; that was how man of the match Chris Harris summed up his outstanding bowling performance in last night's tied one-day cricket international between New Zealand at England at McLean Park.
Harris took three for 20 in 10 overs, bowling three of England's best batsmen -- captain Mike Atherton, Alec Stewart and Nasser Hussain -- with late dipping inswingers.
His wickets came at a critical time when England were starting to get on top in their chase for 238 to win the match, and the five-game series.
Although not his best one-day figures -- they are five for 42 against Pakistan at Sialkot late last year -- Harris admitted it was among his finest performances.
"For me personally it probably ranks right up there," the 27-year-old Canterbury allrounder said last night.
"Ten overs for 20 on what I consider a pretty good wicket and fast outfield, I'm delighted."
Harris has tended towards bowling brisk legspinners in the last two seasons, since the national selectors suggested medium pace inswingers weren't sufficient to rate him a frontline one-day bowler.
The change has worked well, but last night Harris reverted back to his former style, with spectacular results.
"Today conditions suited them. I was able to get the ball to move in the air.
"I've always used it as a variation and here I used it a little more than than I normally would.
"I might bowl a few more of them from now on."
Harris said he had found the ball tends to wobble about in the evening atmosphere at Napier in the past.
Last night confirmed that view, and Harris earned praise from Atherton after the match.
"Chris Harris bowled exceptionally well and got them back in the game," he said.
Harris' performance took his one-day bowling record to 80 wickets in 78 matches, to go with 1290 runs at an average of a tick under 25.
